     2	name: aws-waf-log-analysis
     3	description: >-
     4	  Use this skill when an investigation describes symptoms on a CloudFront distribution, Application
     5	  Load Balancer or API Gateway API and asks what the root cause is or what happened, even if AWS
     6	  WAF is never named: users, partners, webhooks, scripts or mobile apps get HTTP 403, 405 or 202
     7	  responses, empty responses or a 4xx spike; forms, uploads, reviews or listings are rejected; a
     8	  partner integration fails; requests look suspicious or malicious (SQL injection, XSS, scans,
     9	  bots); or an outage or timeouts hit the front door. It checks whether a Web ACL is in the path
     10	  (and continues the RCA when WAF is not the cause), finds which WAF rule, Anti-DDoS rule or Shield
     11	  Advanced mitigation blocked, challenged or only counted the requests and whether that is a false
     12	  positive, an attack or both, and hunts for threats WAF detected but did not block. Uses WAF logs
     13	  (CloudWatch Logs Insights or Athena), metrics and sampled requests; records evidence-backed
     14	  findings, advisory scoped fixes and a threat-hunt report.
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: lkna
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "AWS WAF, AWS Shield, Amazon CloudFront, Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon Athena"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Security, Networking"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# AWS WAF Log Analysis
     24	
     25	Find out whether AWS WAF (including Anti-DDoS rules and Shield Advanced automatic mitigation) caused a front-door symptom, and what it denied (Mode A); or hunt WAF logs for threats, including what WAF detected but did not block (Mode B).
     26	
     27	## Purpose and guarantees
     28	
     29	- **Read-only.** Use only Describe, Get and List calls, plus `logs:StartQuery`/`GetQueryResults`, `athena:StartQueryExecution` (SELECT only, when permitted)/`GetQueryResults`, `cloudtrail:LookupEvents`, `wafv2:GetSampledRequests` and `cloudwatch:GetMetricData`.
     30	- Never run DDL. Never change a Web ACL, rule, IP set, Shield setting, log configuration or any other resource.
     31	- **Advisory.** Describe fixes in prose for a human to review and apply. Never apply them.
     32	- **Single-turn.** Never ask the user a question and never wait for input. Apply "Defaults when input is missing", record every default under "Assumptions", and continue.
     33	- **Never stop on a gap.** A denied call or a missing table moves you to the next source or the degraded path.
     34	- **Exact errors.** Record the exact error code. Call something "not permitted" only on `AccessDenied`/`UnauthorizedOperation`.
     35	  - A cancelled, timed-out or throttled call is retried once, then reported as not completed.
     36	  - A tool refusal such as "service operations are not allowed" means: run the call in a subagent.
     37	- **Records are the deliverable** in both modes (symptoms, observations, findings, gaps, hypotheses); the last message closes them (see "Output").
     38	- **Final output.** Complete as delivered; never ends with a question or an offer. Never call `ask_user` (or any ask tool), not even after the answer to offer follow-up work or a fix: a turn that ends on a tool call loses the answer. Put follow-ups in "Next steps" and end on plain text.
     39	
     40	## Pick the mode from the request
     41	
     42	Inputs: the request text plus any incident or alarm details. A threat hunt needs no alarm. Record the mode under "Assumptions".
     43	
     44	Most requests never name WAF: they describe a symptom on a CloudFront distribution, ALB or API Gateway API and ask for the root cause or what happened. Do D-1 first. No Web ACL in the path: record `WAF_CLEARED` and continue the RCA to the actual cause (A0, "After `WAF_CLEARED`"). Otherwise classify:
     45	
     46	| Request contains | Mode |
     47	|---|---|
     48	| Denial or error symptoms: 403/405/202, empty responses, "blocked", "can't access", rejected forms, uploads or posts, a failing partner, webhook or integration, a 4xx/5xx spike, timeouts, an outage, or an alarm on a front-door resource | **Mode A**, starting with the A0 rule-out |
     49	| Suspicious traffic or hunting language: "malicious", "suspicious requests", "SQL injection", "scan", "attack", "bots", "what happened to these requests", "review WAF logs", "is WAF missing anything", a scheduled or recurring review | **Mode B** |
     50	| Both | Mode A first, then Mode B on the same window, focused on the slice Mode A found |
     51	| Neither, but the incident involves a resource that a Web ACL protects | **A0 rule-out only**; if A0 finds WAF implicated or inconclusive, continue with A1 to A7 |
     52	
     53	Mode A `CORRECT_MITIGATION`: recommend Mode B on that slice, or run it when hunting is in scope.
     54	
     55	## Defaults when input is missing
     56	
     57	Never ask; apply and record the default. Full table: "Defaults when input is missing (full table)" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     58	
     59	- **Time window:** Mode A: incident start minus 30 min through now, capped at 24 h; no incident time: last 3 h. Mode B: last 7 days.
     60	- **Web ACL:** every ACL on the resources in the request; none identifiable: all ACLs (both scopes), top 3 by denying volume.
     61	- **Several tables or log groups:** the exact location match with the newest data.
     62	- **S3 logging but no table, or no logging:** don't stop; take the degraded path and report the gap with the advisory fix.
     63	- **Missing permission:** fall back to the next source and name the permission.
     64	
     65	## Discover
     66	
     67	Read [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md) for D-1 to D-7 at the start of every run. Never ask for a resource or ACL.
     68	
     69	- **D-1 Resource to Web ACL:** CloudFront `GetDistributionConfig` `WebACLId`; regional resources `wafv2:GetWebACLForResource`.
     70	- **D-2 Read the ACL:** `wafv2:GetWebACL` for rule order, actions, managed groups and versions, `RuleActionOverrides`, Count overrides, scope-downs, custom responses, token domains, immunity times, IP set references, and any `ShieldMitigationRuleGroup_*` rule.
     71	- **D-2b Token posture:** classify P0 (no token-aware rules), P1 (token labels, no or only threshold-based enforcement) or P2 (strict token enforcement); confirm with Q-18.
     72	- **D-3 Log destination:** `wafv2:GetLoggingConfiguration`, including logging filters and redacted fields. Log group: Logs Insights. S3 or Firehose to S3: Athena. None, or a non-S3 destination without a full S3 backup: degraded path.
     73	- **D-4 Find the table or log group:** list tables in **every** Glue database, including `default`, across the Regions in D-4. Write "no table" only after that full listing. Never analyze raw log objects (`s3:GetObject`) as a substitute.
     74	- **D-7 Shield Advanced status:** `shield:DescribeSubscription`, `DescribeProtection` (L7AM status and action), `ListAttacks`/`DescribeAttack`, and `DDoSDetected` in `AWS/DDoSProtection`.
     75	
     76	**Region rule.** For CloudFront scope, the ACL, its logging configuration, its log group and its `AWS/WAFV2` metrics are in us-east-1. Only the Glue table and Athena follow the customer's setup; run Athena in the table's Region.
     77	
     78	## Bind schema and guard cost
     79	
     80	Queries are cited as `Q-NN (QA-NN / QI-NN)`; run the one for the backend from D-3 and D-4. Detail: "Schema binding and cost guards (detail)" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     81	
     82	- **Athena:** bind `<table>`, `<req>`, label type and `<pf>` from `glue:GetTable`. The log subagent reads [athena-queries.md](references/athena-queries.md) "Schema binding" and the query sections it runs.
     83	- **Logs Insights:** the log subagent reads [logs-insights-queries.md](references/logs-insights-queries.md) "Conventions" and the query sections it runs.
     84	- **Probe first, in the log subagent.** The main agent runs no Athena query. On a probe error, take the degraded path.
     85	- **Cost:** prune partitions, start narrow, no unbounded `SELECT *`, at most one `UNNEST` per query.
     86	- **Budget:** about 15 log queries (about 10 on the Mode B fast path). Report queries run and bytes scanned.
     87	
     88	## Run it in AWS DevOps Agent
     89	
     90	The main agent discovers; subagents query. Read "Subagent briefs" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md) before you start a log subagent, and when your prompt says discovery is done.
     91	
     92	**If your prompt says discovery is done and you are a subagent:** skip Steps 1 to 3, start no further subagents and do not load this skill again. Follow "Subagent briefs" for your role.
     93	
     94	**If you are a subagent without a discovery brief** (the platform handed you the whole task, so no main agent ran Steps 1 to 3): do the main agent's and the log subagent's work yourself, and start no further log subagent.
     95	
     96	1. Do D-1 to D-4. For D-4, call `glue:GetTables` on every database that `glue:GetDatabases` returns, including `default`, and match `Location` to the log prefix. A database list alone never means "no table".
     97	2. Never analyze raw S3 log objects, or sampled requests for a window that ended over 3 hours ago.
     98	3. Run the probe, then the mode's queries. Copy each query verbatim from [athena-queries.md](references/athena-queries.md) or [logs-insights-queries.md](references/logs-insights-queries.md) by searching for its ID (for example `QA-13b`). Never summarize the query references with a distill tool: summaries drop mandatory queries.
     99	4. In Mode B, run Q-13b and Q-19 whatever else you run. In both modes, run Q-20 for a sub-rule that matches payloads (blocking or in Count).
     100	5. Return the full Output block, so the agent that started you can pass it on verbatim.
     101	
     102	- [ ] Step 1: **Main agent: discover, bind, delegate.**
     103	  - Load this skill once and no other log-search or log-analysis skill. Read reference sections by search or offset.
     104	  - Do D-1 to D-4, D-2b and `glue:GetTable` (or find the log group) yourself.
     105	  - Start **one** log-analysis subagent (`preloaded_skills: ['aws-waf-log-analysis']` where supported) and the change subagent (Step 3) in the same turn.
     106	  - The brief carries everything bound, the mode and steps, the budget and the return format; neutral wording; a unique `name` per launch.
     107	- [ ] Step 2: **Main agent: no query libraries, no log queries.** Do metrics (A1, D-5) and Shield (D-7) while the subagent runs. At most one follow-up log pass, for a new uncharacterized candidate.
     108	- [ ] Step 3: **CloudTrail only in a change subagent, never in the main agent.**
     109	  - Every `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` (A5; "After `WAF_CLEARED`"; Mode B change correlation) runs in one change subagent.
     110	  - Launch: `agent_type` `generic`, `name` `change-timeline`, `preloaded_skills: ['aws-waf-log-analysis', 'investigating-infrastructure-changes']` (whichever are available).
     111	  - Always start it, even when memory or an earlier refusal says CloudTrail is blocked; mandatory for a rule-out request.
     112	  - Its prompt points it to "Change lookups" in [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) (Regions, event names, sweep, return contract).
     113	  - Write "blocked" or "denied" only on the change subagent's own `AccessDenied`.
     114	  - No completed lookup: write "changes: not checked (<reason>)". Never "no change", "ruled out" or "CloudTrail is blocked in this environment".
     115	- [ ] Step 4: **Subagents return compact aggregates only.** Per query: ID, row count, bytes scanned, about 20 top rows; payloads as class and count; never raw result sets or log records.
     116	- [ ] Step 5: **Refusal, failure or no subagent capability.**
     117	  - Relaunch a refused log or change subagent once, under a new name, with the same `preloaded_skills`.
     118	  - Change relaunch fails too: "changes: not checked (change subagent refused twice)".
     119	  - Log relaunch fails too, or no subagents: run about 10 count-only aggregate queries yourself and record the fallback.
     120	  - A3/A4 detail is then out of reach: say so and cap confidence at "low".
     121	
     122	## Rule and label knowledge
     123	
     124	Read L-1 in [label-reference.md](references/label-reference.md) when you need a rule or label meaning (in AWS DevOps Agent, inside the log subagent).
     125	
     126	- Order: `wafv2:DescribeManagedRuleGroup` with the ACL's version when permitted (opt-in; record a denial). Then exact label strings from Q-09 (casing can differ from rule names). Then the bundled, dated tables.
     127	- A connected AWS documentation tool may confirm semantics; never required.
     128	- A label found in neither the API output nor the bundled tables is "meaning unverified". Never infer meaning from its name.
     129	
     130	## Mode A: access-denied triage
     131	
     132	Read [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) when Mode A runs (step detail), and [remediation-patterns.md](references/remediation-patterns.md) (R-01 to R-11) at Step A7.
     133	
     134	- [ ] Step A0: **WAF rule-out**, cheapest first: Web ACL in the path; symptom type fits WAF; denying metrics and Shield or Anti-DDoS signals rose; Q-15 shows denials on the scope.
     135	  - Wording alone never clears WAF (a 202 with an empty body is often reported as "timeout").
     136	  - Only "no Web ACL in the path" stops the WAF checks at once; the change subagent still runs the origin-side checks.
     137	  - `WAF_CLEARED` never ends the RCA. Origin-side next steps are checks, not conclusions; name no root cause outside WAF that evidence does not show. An origin-side change whose time matches onset and recovery is the Root Cause, with the event evidence and load-balancer metrics; never stop at "out of scope".
     138	- [ ] Step A1: **Confirm involvement:** front-door 4xx versus `AWS/WAFV2` Blocked/Challenge/Captcha per rule, against the preceding window and the prior day, with request-volume stability. Never clear WAF on 4xx alone.
     139	- [ ] Step A2: **Attribute:** group terminating records by action, rule, managed sub-rule, response code and time bucket (Q-02, Q-01, Q-14 for Shield L7AM).
     140	- [ ] Step A3: **Client capability (Challenge/CAPTCHA only):** token posture and the path's token-status profile (Q-18, Q-05, Q-09, Q-04). Quote the `failureReason` value with its count (for example `TOKEN_MISSING`).
     141	- [ ] Step A4: **Profile who is affected:** clients, URIs and match details against allowed history before onset (Q-03, Q-04, Q-06, Q-07, Q-10, Q-12, Q-13). For blocked attackers, run Q-19; never "benign" without it.
     142	  - One profile per affected client or population (Q-21): IP, user agent, country (ASN if logged), paths, blocked and allowed counts, first and last seen. Report the measured distinct client count; never assume distributed or single-source traffic.
     143	  - IP-set rule denies: read the set (`wafv2:GetIPSet`), name the matching entry, and say whether a similarly named allow set exists and which rule references it.
     144	- [ ] Step A5: **Correlate changes and events:** CloudTrail (change subagent), managed group versions, Anti-DDoS `event-detected` onset, Shield attacks (D-7). A version change or association is a cause only under the A5 evidence rules. No completed lookup: "changes: not checked".
     145	- [ ] Step A6: **Verdict** per denying (rule, action) pair: `FALSE_POSITIVE`, `CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE`, `CORRECT_MITIGATION` or `MIXED`; or overall `WAF_CLEARED` or `INCONCLUSIVE`. Give confidence (high, likely, low) and quantified impact. When legitimate users are reported denied and the logs cannot split a sub-rule's matches, the pair is `MIXED` (likely), never `CORRECT_MITIGATION`; judge request patterns, not whole clients.
     146	  - Missing allowed history is not evidence of attack. A monitor, health checker or integration with a benign profile hit by a header-presence or size rule is `FALSE_POSITIVE` (likely), with owner confirmation under "Verify before acting".
     147	  - **Payload split:** when a sub-rule (blocking or in Count) matches payloads, group its matches by pattern and field (Q-20), classify each pattern as attack or legitimate content (business text that only looks like SQL, script or JNDI), and report the split with counts ("Payload split inside one sub-rule" in [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md)).
     148	- [ ] Step A7: **Advise:** the narrowest R-xx fix, marked *reduces* or *eliminates*, validated in Count first (straight to Block only as R-01's labelled alternative).
     149	  - `CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE`: first a path scope-down of the challenge rule (R-05, covering every observed non-HTML path, including `/`), or token/SDK integration (R-06). Both rank above R-04.
     150	  - An IP or path is only a scope-down or exclusion on the challenge rule itself. Never add the client to an IP set used by an Allow-action rule.
     151	  - Never offer removing or disabling the Web ACL.
     152	
     153	## Mode B: threat hunting
     154	
     155	Read [threat-hunting.md](references/threat-hunting.md) when Mode B runs; classify with [threat-taxonomy.md](references/threat-taxonomy.md) at Step B6. Detected-not-blocked is a priority finding (threat labels on ALLOW, Count-mode matches, rate rules in Count, attacker residue). A logging filter that drops ALLOW records limits the analysis: say so.
     156	
     157	- [ ] Step B1: **Fast path first** for a window of 2 hours or less, or one specific question: about 10 fixed queries, started together, polled once. The full set is in "Fast path".
     158	  - Q-13b is mandatory. It sets the top talker apart so a short burst cannot hide.
     159	  - Every sensitive-path burst and every client over a rate-rule limit is a finding with method, URI, count, peaks and first to last seen. Never "ordinary", "normal" or "a retry burst".
     160	  - Run the full funnel only for candidates the fast path cannot settle.
     161	- [ ] Step B2: **B0 Known automation:** high-volume, low-diversity clients with corroboration, excluded from baselines (Q-13, Q-12, Q-01). Report them under a required "Known automation" heading. Never label them card testing or abuse. Never exclude a population with token-reuse or coordinated-activity labels.
     162	- [ ] Step B3: **B-A Overview and B-B Standouts:** time series, breakdowns and label frequency (Q-01, Q-02, Q-03, Q-09); then standouts ranked numerically (Q-08, Q-11, Q-12, Q-14, Q-16b, Q-17).
     163	- [ ] Step B4: **Attacker residue (B-B):** for every client with any BLOCK from an injection, bad-input or bot rule, report its ALLOW requests as a missed-by-rule finding (Q-19).
     164	  - Never "benign", "clean" or "accounted for" unless Q-19 showed `args_class` `none` on application paths.
     165	  - Explain a miss only from the rule's documented inspection target (L-1); otherwise "reason not determined".
     166	  - Copy the field location verbatim. A query-argument residue needs a query-string rule; a `UriPath` rule does not cover it.
     167	  - **Count-mode payload split:** for every injection or bad-input sub-rule in Count, run Q-20 and split its matches by pattern and field: the attack part is "detected, not blocked"; the legitimate-content part is a false positive that must stay unblocked.
     168	- [ ] Step B5: **B-C to B-E Drill, narrow, confirm:** re-pivot one standout; one line per Count or rate-rule client (Q-08c); narrow to one client, rule or endpoint; confirm with Q-10 or Q-16b/Q-16.
     169	  - A burst on a payment, checkout, login, signup or password-reset URI is a card-testing or credential-stuffing finding whatever its size. Fix it with a path-scoped R-10 on that URI, Count first.
     170	- [ ] Step B6: **B-F and B-G:** resolve load-bearing labels (L-1; unverified stays unverified), map each signature to a class and an R-xx mitigation, and hand legitimate-user denials to Mode A.
     171	- [ ] Step B7: **Record, then generate the hunting report.** Write the Mode B records first ("Records" under "Output"). If the runtime can create a report artifact, write the report as a Markdown artifact, following the section order and tables of [assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md](assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md) exactly; load it first:
     172	  ```
     173	  read_skill_resource(skill_id="aws-waf-log-analysis", path="assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md")
     174	  ```
     175	  - The records stay the primary deliverable; the report repeats their numbers and adds no finding.
     176	  - No artifact capability: put the same sections into the final message, after the Output template block.
     177	  - **If the `read_skill_resource` call fails**, note at the top of the report "report template (`assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md`) could not be loaded; structure follows the Mode B contract", and still produce the sections of "Output (Mode B contract)" in [threat-hunting.md](references/threat-hunting.md).
     178	
     179	## Degraded path
     180	
     181	Use when WAF logs can't be queried (no table, no logging, a non-S3 destination, a missing permission); the investigation continues. Read D-5 in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     182	
     183	- **WAF metrics** say *whether* WAF denied and *which rule*, not *who* or *which path*. **Sampled requests:** last 3 hours only, examples rather than counts.
     184	- **Confidence:** cap at "likely" (A0 structural clears can be high). With Shield L7AM attached, a metric-based clear is `INCONCLUSIVE`. Lower to "low" when A3 or A4 cannot be assessed.
     185	- **Wrap-up:** state that WAF logs weren't analyzed and why, with the advisory fix (D-6 DDL, logging configuration, or the missing permission).
     186	
     187	## Output
     188	
     189	Read [output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md) before you write any record, handoff or final answer (record rules, last-message rules, mitigation handoff). Mode sections are in the mode references.
     190	
     191	**Template.** The main agent's very last message closes the investigation, in every mode and verdict, including any reply after the mitigation step. It starts with `Assumptions:` (no preface) and repeats this block even if earlier messages carried it:
     192	
     193	```
     194	Assumptions: window; Web ACLs; backend; mode; defaults, fallbacks, calls not completed (exact error)
     195	Verdict: <Mode A: per (rule, action), or WAF_CLEARED / INCONCLUSIVE; Mode B: per confirmed finding> (confidence: high | likely | low)
     196	Evidence: <key numbers from the log subagent's table (step-5 fallback: your recorded results), with query IDs>; Changes (CloudTrail): <per category, Regions/sources/names searched: events found | none found>; origin-side: not checked (<reason>) if not searched | not checked (<reason>) | not applicable (Mode B)
     197	AI-generated: findings need human verification before anyone acts on them.
     198	```
     199	
     200	Then the mode sections, the findings, the next steps, and a last line `Ruled out: <each hypothesis, with the evidence that closed it, or "still open">`.
     201	
     202	**Counts.** Copy every count from the log subagent's table; never recompute or round. Memory is never evidence.
     203	
     204	**Records.** Platform records are the judged deliverable in both modes. In both:
     205	
     206	- one observation record per key result first (counts, window, baseline, query ID), so findings can cite them;
     207	- exactly one Root Cause;
     208	- every Cause and Root Cause finding lists those observation IDs in its supporting observations (never empty) and the Web ACL in its related resources;
     209	- a gap record per denied or not-completed call or unassessed step; closed hypotheses with their evidence.
     210	
     211	Mode A: one symptom per burst and per affected client or population (IP, user agent, paths, blocked and allowed counts, first and last seen; never merge clients or rules); one Cause per denying (rule, action) pair, titled with the exact rule and sub-rule ID and the verdict, naming the matching resource (IP set and entry).
     212	
     213	Both modes: a payload split gives one Cause per (sub-rule, verdict), or one `MIXED` Cause listing both parts with counts, field and pattern summary.
     214	
     215	Mode B (full rules in "Mode B records" in [output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md)):
     216	
     217	- one Symptom per distinct activity pattern: window, client, method and path, counts;
     218	- one Cause per confirmed threat finding, titled with class, client and exact rule and sub-rule IDs, or "not matched by any rule", or "detected, not blocked: <rate rule> in Count";
     219	- known automation as an observation plus a closed hypothesis, never a threat finding;
     220	- the Root Cause is the overall assessment: what WAF caught, what it missed and why (for example a rate rule in Count), naming every Cause, linking their observations and any known-automation observation, with WAF-layer and Application-layer mitigations (path-scoped R-10 first for card testing; when known automation exceeds the site-wide rate rule, one sentence that it stays in Count and why).
     221	
     222	**Mitigation guardrails** (every message, finding and handoff):
     223	
     224	- Never disable or remove a rule group or the Web ACL.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Rejected form submissions (403)
**Description:** Users' form POST submissions rejected with 403 at the CloudFront front door during 17:30–17:50 UTC.
**Time:** 2026-10-06T17:30:00Z - 2026-10-06T17:50:00Z

### Front-door 403s on no-User-Agent requests
**Description:** A later batch of front-door requests with no User-Agent header blocked with 403 during 18:05–18:25 UTC.
**Time:** 2026-10-06T18:05:00Z - 2026-10-06T18:25:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: SizeRestrictions_BODY blocking oversized form bodies
**Description:** Mechanism confirmed: a **single client (198.51.100.80, US)** with a normal Chrome User-Agent and JA4 `t13d591000_a33745022dd6_1f22a2ca17c4` sent **1200 oversized POST /checkout requests** whose bodies (up to **10,185 B**) exceed the CRS **SizeRestrictions_BODY 8 KB (8192 B)** inspection/block limit, returning **403** — the rejected form submissions (17:30–17:50 UTC). Typical /checkout bodies are only ~125 B, so these are anomalously large.
**Cascades to:** symptom-rejected-forms

### Cause: NoUserAgent_HEADER blocking no-UA requests
**Description:** Mechanism confirmed: a **single client (198.51.100.70, US)** with **no User-Agent header**, sharing the **same JA4 `t13d591000_a33745022dd6_1f22a2ca17c4`** as the Phase-1 client, sent **599 GET /home + /catalog requests** blocked by CRS **NoUserAgent_HEADER** returning **403** — the front-door 403s (18:05–18:25 UTC). The equal-count AntiDDoS `challengeable-request` label is non-terminating/incidental.
**Cascades to:** symptom-frontdoor-403

### Root Cause: CommonRuleSet default-Block produces two false positives on legitimate traffic
**Description:** AWS Managed Rules CommonRuleSet (priority 3, default Block action, no RuleActionOverrides) produced two independent false positives in one window against legitimate traffic — SizeRestrictions_BODY rejecting oversize /checkout form POSTs (bodies up to 10,185 B > the 8 KB CRS limit), and NoUserAgent_HEADER rejecting a UA-less automated client on /home + /catalog. No configuration change occurred (CloudTrail clean over ~42h; rules already in Block) and request volume was flat (~11k/5min), so the trigger was an input/traffic-composition change — a burst of legitimate automated traffic whose request shapes those two CRS sub-rules reject by default — not a deployment or config change. Both blocked populations share the identical JA4 fingerprint t13d591000_a33745022dd6_1f22a2ca17c4 and originate from AWS us-west-2 ranges, indicating a single legitimate automation harness.
**Cascades to:** finding-size-body, finding-no-ua

#### Supporting Observations
- **Phase 1 client profile: single IP, oversized /checkout POST bodies:** QA-03 (SizeRestrictions_BODY) resolves Wave 1 to a **single client IP 198.51.100.80 (US)** with a normal browser User-Agent (`Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ... Chrome/141.0.0.0 Safari/537.36`), JA4 `t13d591000_a33745022dd6_1f22a2ca17c4`, all **POST /checkout**, **1200 requests** — all BLOCKed (403).

QA-07 body-size distribution (ALLOWED baseline, requestbodysize>0) shows **/checkout** bodies are typically tiny (p50 ~125 B) but reach a **max of 10,185 B** (inspected 10,185) — above the CRS **SizeRestrictions_BODY 8 KB (8192 B)** body-inspection/block limit. Other paths stay small (/cart 46 B, /checkout/payment 74 B, /checkout/delivery 19 B). The Phase-1 client's 1200 oversized POST /checkout requests are the ones exceeding the limit.
- **Phase 2 client profile: single IP, missing User-Agent header:** QA-03 (NoUserAgent_HEADER) resolves Wave 2 to a **single client IP 198.51.100.70 (US)** with the **User-Agent header ABSENT (empty)**, sharing the **SAME JA4 `t13d591000_a33745022dd6_1f22a2ca17c4`** as the Phase-1 client. Requests: GET /home (300) + GET /catalog (299) = **599 requests** — all BLOCKed (403) by NoUserAgent_HEADER.

The shared JA4 ties both waves to **one client tooling/software** despite the two distinct source IPs; the distinct IPs and distinct rule triggers are why they surfaced as two separate symptoms.
- **SQLi/XSS/KnownBadInputs rules: zero blocks in window:** AWS-AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet, CrossSiteScripting_QUERYARGUMENTS, and AWS-AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet all returned zero BlockedRequests across the 16:00–18:45 UTC window. The incident is confined to two CommonRuleSet sub-rules; attack-signature rules did not contribute.

## Other Gaps

### Owning identity of the two client IPs not determinable from WAF logs
**Description:** The owning team/identity behind IPs 198.51.100.80 / 198.51.100.70 (same JA4 fingerprint t13d591000_a33745022dd6_1f22a2ca17c4, both in AWS us-west-2 ranges) is NOT determinable from WAF logs alone. Confirming they are expected internal/partner automation would finalize both false-positive verdicts at high confidence. This does NOT change the root cause — both CommonRuleSet blocks remain confirmed false positives against legitimate traffic regardless of the owner lookup.

### Shield Advanced not subscribed; L7 automatic mitigation unavailable
**Description:** shield.describe_subscription returned ResourceNotFoundException for account 012345678901_1 — Shield Advanced is not active. This rules out Shield L7 automatic mitigation as a cause and means AntiDDoS behavior comes solely from the AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet in the Web ACL. Not blocking, but noted for mitigation scoping.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Apply two scoped, per-sub-rule tuning changes to the CloudFront Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, each deployed in Count first and only then switched to Block: (1) override SizeRestrictions_BODY to Count and add a label rule that blocks on the SizeRestrictions_Body label everywhere EXCEPT POST /checkout; (2) override NoUserAgent_HEADER to Count and add a label rule that blocks on the NoUserAgent_Header label everywhere EXCEPT verified automation IPs on GET /home and /catalog. No managed group or other sub-rule is disabled. Advisory WAF tuning — no prior config change to roll back.

## Reasoning
Two independent false positives in the same CommonRuleSet (priority 3, default Block, no overrides) returned 403 to legitimate traffic 17:30–18:30 UTC on 2026-10-06. Volume was flat and CloudTrail was clean over ~42h, so this is tuning, not a rollback. Each fix is scoped to one sub-rule, path and field so protection elsewhere is unchanged. Both verdicts are 'likely' false positives pending owner confirmation of the two source IPs (198.51.100.80, 198.51.100.70; shared JA4, AWS us-west-2).

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Snapshot the full Rules array + LockToken as the rollback baseline…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Snapshot the full Rules array + LockToken as the rollback baseline; confirm CommonRuleSet has OverrideAction None and no RuleActionOverrides.

#### 1.2 Confirm the two source IPs are legitimate automation before applying…
**Type:** text
Owner confirmation required before loosening anything: verify that source IPs 198.51.100.80 and 198.51.100.70 — which share JA4 fingerprint t13d591000_a33745022dd6_1f22a2ca17c4 and an AWS us-west-2 origin — are a known, legitimate automation harness and not attacker-controlled. Do not proceed to apply until confirmed.
**Purpose:** Confirm the two source IPs are legitimate automation before applying any exception.
**Risks:** If the IPs are not legitimate, the NoUserAgent_HEADER IP-scoped exception would exempt an attacker-controlled client from the no-User-Agent protection on /home and /catalog.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Re-read to confirm no concurrent edits and capture a fresh LockToken…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Re-read to confirm no concurrent edits and capture a fresh LockToken for the apply call.
**Advisory:** WAF requires the current LockToken on update-web-acl; a stale token fails safely with WAFOptimisticLockException.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Remove the SizeRestrictions_BODY false positive on large POST /checkout…
**Type:** text
Cause 1 (SizeRestrictions_BODY): in one update-web-acl call, (a) add a RuleActionOverride setting ONLY SizeRestrictions_BODY to Count on the priority-3 CommonRuleSet; (b) add a new custom rule after the group (priority 6) matching label awswaf:managed:aws:core-rule-set:SizeRestrictions_Body AND NOT (URI /checkout AND method POST), deployed with action COUNT; leave all other sub-rules at Block.
**Purpose:** Remove the SizeRestrictions_BODY false positive on large POST /checkout bodies while keeping body-size protection on every other path.
**Risks:** Between overriding the sub-rule to Count and switching the label rule to Block, body-size protection is reduced site-wide — keep the window short., Raising AssociationConfig.RequestBody would NOT fix this: it does not change the 8 KB SizeRestrictions_BODY threshold.
**Advisory:** Copy the label verbatim; label casing (SizeRestrictions_Body) differs from the rule name (SizeRestrictions_BODY).

#### 3.2 Remove the NoUserAgent_HEADER false positive for the verified UA-less…
**Type:** text
Cause 2 (NoUserAgent_HEADER): in one update-web-acl call, (a) add a RuleActionOverride setting ONLY NoUserAgent_HEADER to Count; (b) create an IP set (us-east-1/CloudFront) with the owner-verified egress IPs 198.51.100.80/32 and 198.51.100.70/32; (c) add a new custom rule after the group (priority 7) matching label awswaf:managed:aws:core-rule-set:NoUserAgent_Header AND NOT (source IP in that set AND URI /home or /catalog AND method GET), deployed with action COUNT; do NOT add these IPs to any Allow rule (Allow is terminating).
**Purpose:** Remove the NoUserAgent_HEADER false positive for the verified UA-less automation on GET /home and /catalog while keeping the protection everywhere else.
**Risks:** AWS egress IPs can change — review the IP set regularly with the owner., Between Count override and label-rule Block switch, NoUserAgent_HEADER protection is reduced site-wide — keep the window short.
**Advisory:** Scoping to the IP set AND the two GET paths keeps the exception as narrow as the observed pattern.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm only SizeRestrictions_BODY and NoUserAgent_HEADER are Count…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Confirm only SizeRestrictions_BODY and NoUserAgent_HEADER are Count, the two label rules exist at priorities 6/7, and everything else stays at default Block.

#### 4.2 Prove each enforcement rule is correctly scoped in Count before…
**Type:** text
Count-first validation: over a representative traffic cycle (get-sampled-requests plus the new rules' CountedRequests CloudWatch metrics), confirm each label rule counts out-of-scope labelled requests and ZERO legitimate in-scope traffic (no legitimate /checkout POSTs; none of the automation's GET /home and /catalog). Only then switch each label rule's action from Count to Block one at a time, watching BlockedRequests and the exempted scopes closely.
**Purpose:** Prove each enforcement rule is correctly scoped in Count before switching it to Block.
**Risks:** Switching to Block before the Count review could re-introduce false positives on legitimate /checkout and automation traffic.
**Advisory:** get-sampled-requests covers only the last 3 hours; use CloudWatch CountedRequests for a longer window.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Revert the Web ACL to its exact pre-change state if the scoped…
**Type:** text
If either label rule misbehaves (blocks legitimate traffic, or leaves protection off outside its intended scope), re-apply the exact baseline Rules array captured in the prepare phase using a fresh LockToken. This removes the two RuleActionOverrides and the two added custom rules (priorities 6 and 7), returning AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet to OverrideAction None with no overrides. Optionally delete the automation IP set once no rule references it.
**Purpose:** Revert the Web ACL to its exact pre-change state if the scoped exceptions cause any problem.
**Risks:** Reverting restores the original false-positive blocking until a corrected exception is applied.
**Advisory:** Rollback requires a current LockToken; re-read the Web ACL first if the saved token is stale.

You are the log-analysis subagent for a Mode A AWS WAF investigation. DISCOVERY IS DONE — do NOT re-run discovery, do NOT start further subagents, do NOT load any other log skill. Follow the "Subagent briefs" guidance in your preloaded aws-waf-log-analysis skill for the log-analysis role, and copy each Athena query VERBATIM from references/athena-queries.md by its ID.

## Incident
Between 17:30 and 18:30 UTC on 2026-10-06, on CloudFront distribution d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net (distribution EEXAMPLE000001), some customers could not submit forms and some automated clients received HTTP 403 responses. Investigative question: which WAF rule(s)/sub-rule(s) terminated these requests, who was affected, and is each a false positive or a correct mitigation?

## Bound schema (use exactly)
- AWS account: 012345678901_1
- Athena/Glue: database `default`, table `waf_logs`, run Athena in region **us-east-1**.
- Table location: s3://aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1/AWSLogs/012345678901_1/WAFLogs/cloudfront/CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4
- Partition key: `log_time` (string). PROBE partitions first (e.g. SHOW PARTITIONS, or inspect partition projection in glue:GetTable Parameters) before querying, and prune to the incident partitions. If a probe query errors, take the degraded path and report the exact error.
- SerDe: org.openx.data.jsonserde.JsonSerDe. Request fields are under `httprequest` struct (clientip, country, headers[], uri, args, httpmethod, host, requestid). Other useful columns: `action`, `terminatingruleid`, `terminatingruletype`, `responsecodesent`, `rulegrouplist` (array of struct with nonterminatingmatchingrules), `labels` (array<struct<name>>), `requestbodysize`, `requestbodysizeinspectedbywaf`, `oversizefields`, `ja3fingerprint`.
- Web ACL: CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 (ARN [redacted ARN]). DefaultAction Allow. Rules in priority order: (0) AWS-AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet [Challenge enabled, exempts /api/ and static assets], (1) AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront [Count only, 300/5min per IP], (2) AWS-AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList, (3) AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, (4) AWS-AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet, (5) AWS-AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet. No RuleActionOverrides, no Count overrides on managed groups.

## Time windows (UTC, 2026-10-06)
- Incident: 17:30:00–18:30:00. Use a lead buffer back to 17:00:00.
- Baseline: preceding window 16:00:00–17:30:00 (same day). If cheap, also sample the prior day 2026-10-05 17:00:00–18:30:00.
- Bucket terminating activity by 5-minute buckets to show onset/offset.

## What CloudWatch metrics already show (confirm or refute with logs — do not just repeat)
- Phase 1 (17:30–17:50): CommonRuleSet sub-rule SizeRestrictions_BODY BlockedRequests 170/300/300/300/130 per 5min.
- Phase 2 (18:05–18:25): CommonRuleSet sub-rule NoUserAgent_HEADER BlockedRequests 126/150/150/149/24 per 5min, with an identical-count anti-ddos label `challengeable-request` blocked series.
- No blocks from SQLiRuleSet, KnownBadInputs, IpReputation, or AntiDDoS-as-terminating-rule in the window per metrics. Rate rule Count-only, flat ~11k/5min (background).

## Required analysis (Mode A, steps A2–A4, A6)
Run the VERBATIM athena-queries.md queries that match these needs; at minimum:
1. **Attribution (Q-02 / Q-01 / Q-14 equivalents):** group terminating records in the incident window by action, terminatingruleid, terminating managed sub-rule, responsecodesent, and 5-min bucket. Confirm the two phases and the exact terminating rule+sub-rule for each, and the response code sent (expected 403). Report which rule TERMINATED (vs merely labeled) — in particular whether AWS-AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet terminated anything or only added the `challengeable-request` label while CommonRuleSet NoUserAgent_HEADER terminated.
2. **Profile Phase 1 (forms, 17:30–17:50):** for SizeRestrictions_BODY blocks — distinct client IP count, top IPs, user agents, countries, httpmethod (expect POST), URIs/host (expect form-submit paths), requestbodysize vs requestbodysizeinspectedbywaf, oversizefields, blocked vs allowed counts, first/last seen. Determine whether these are legitimate large form submissions (benign, diverse clients, normal browser UAs) or an attack.
3. **Profile Phase 2 (automated clients 403, 18:05–18:25):** for NoUserAgent_HEADER blocks — distinct client IP count, top IPs, user-agent header (expect missing/empty), countries, httpmethod, URIs/host, ja3 if present, blocked vs allowed counts, first/last seen. Determine whether these are legitimate automated/API clients lacking a User-Agent (benign) or malicious bots.
4. **Attacker-residue / false-positive test (Q-19, and Q-20 ONLY if a payload-matching sub-rule appears):** for the clients blocked in each phase, report any ALLOW requests and whether any injection/bad-input/bot labels (SQLi, XSS, LFI, Log4J, BadBots) appear on their traffic. Neither SizeRestrictions_BODY nor NoUserAgent_HEADER inspects payloads, so a payload split (Q-20) is likely N/A — but run Q-19 to justify any "benign"/false-positive verdict with data. Never call a population benign without Q-19.
5. **Verdict (A6) per terminating (rule, action) pair:** FALSE_POSITIVE / CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE / CORRECT_MITIGATION / MIXED, with confidence and quantified impact (distinct clients, total blocked requests per phase).

## Budget & return format
- About 10–15 Athena queries max. Prune partitions, start narrow, no unbounded SELECT *, at most one UNNEST per query. Apply the skill's defang rule to any payload/matched-data and redact token/cookie/authorization values.
- Return COMPACT AGGREGATES only: per query — the query ID, row count, bytes scanned, and ~20 top rows. Payloads as class + count only. No raw log records.
- End with the skill's Output block (Assumptions / Verdict per (rule,action) / Evidence with query IDs and counts / Ruled out), plus one client/population profile per affected phase (IPs, UA, countries, paths, methods, blocked+allowed counts, first/last seen, distinct client count).", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

# Discovery, Log Sources, Degraded Path and Advisory DDL

Procedures D-1 to D-7 take the agent from "something is denying traffic" to the Web ACL, its configuration, its log destination and the queryable backend. Every procedure is read-only. The agent never creates, alters or deletes a resource, and it never runs DDL.

**Rules for every procedure**

- Never stop the investigation because a call is denied or returns nothing. Record the gap, apply the stated fallback and move on (D-5 is the shared fallback).

     212	**Use when:** you have a `<focus_label>` and want to see whether it travels with other labels, forming a signature.

     217	  WHERE <pf>
     218	    AND contains(transform(labels, x -> x.name), '<focus_label>'))

     290	b AS (

     292	         count_if(action = 'ALLOW') AS allowed, min(ts) AS t0, max(ts) AS t1
     293	  FROM k GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
     294	p AS (
     295	  SELECT b.*, sum(n) OVER (PARTITION BY client_ip, scope, method, uri, floor(b1 / 5)) AS n5 FROM b),

     299	         from_unixtime(min(t0) / 1000) AS first_seen, from_unixtime(max(t1) / 1000) AS last_seen

  - cloudfront.amazonaws.com: UpdateDistribution, AssociateWebACL / changes to WebACLId on EEXAMPLE000001.
  - Any change that pinned/updated the AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet version (which governs SizeRestrictions_BODY and NoUserAgent_HEADER behavior).
- For each relevant event: eventTime, eventName, eventSource, user identity (who), source IP, and the request parameters that changed (especially action overrides / versions).

## Return contract
- A compact timeline of relevant events (or "none found") with eventTime, eventName, who, and what changed.
- Explicitly state per category: "events found" (list) or "none found", and the exact Regions/sources/event names searched.
- If any lookup is denied, report the exact error code (AccessDenied etc.). If CloudTrail cannot be queried at all, say "changes: not checked (<reason>)" — never claim "no change" without a completed lookup.

     2	name: aws-waf-log-analysis
     3	description: >-
     4	  Use this skill when an investigation describes symptoms on a CloudFront distribution, Application
     5	  Load Balancer or API Gateway API and asks what the root cause is or what happened, even if AWS
     6	  WAF is never named: users, partners, webhooks, scripts or mobile apps get HTTP 403, 405 or 202
     7	  responses, empty responses or a 4xx spike; forms, uploads, reviews or listings are rejected; a
     8	  partner integration fails; requests look suspicious or malicious (SQL injection, XSS, scans,
     9	  bots); or an outage or timeouts hit the front door. It checks whether a Web ACL is in the path
     10	  (and continues the RCA when WAF is not the cause), finds which WAF rule, Anti-DDoS rule or Shield
     11	  Advanced mitigation blocked, challenged or only counted the requests and whether that is a false
     12	  positive, an attack or both, and hunts for threats WAF detected but did not block. Uses WAF logs
     13	  (CloudWatch Logs Insights or Athena), metrics and sampled requests; records evidence-backed
     14	  findings, advisory scoped fixes and a threat-hunt report.
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: lkna
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "AWS WAF, AWS Shield, Amazon CloudFront, Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon Athena"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Security, Networking"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# AWS WAF Log Analysis
     24	
     25	Find out whether AWS WAF (including Anti-DDoS rules and Shield Advanced automatic mitigation) caused a front-door symptom, and what it denied (Mode A); or hunt WAF logs for threats, including what WAF detected but did not block (Mode B).
     26	
     27	## Purpose and guarantees
     28	
     29	- **Read-only.** Use only Describe, Get and List calls, plus `logs:StartQuery`/`GetQueryResults`, `athena:StartQueryExecution` (SELECT only, when permitted)/`GetQueryResults`, `cloudtrail:LookupEvents`, `wafv2:GetSampledRequests` and `cloudwatch:GetMetricData`.
     30	- Never run DDL. Never change a Web ACL, rule, IP set, Shield setting, log configuration or any other resource.
     31	- **Advisory.** Describe fixes in prose for a human to review and apply. Never apply them.
     32	- **Single-turn.** Never ask the user a question and never wait for input. Apply "Defaults when input is missing", record every default under "Assumptions", and continue.
     33	- **Never stop on a gap.** A denied call or a missing table moves you to the next source or the degraded path.
     34	- **Exact errors.** Record the exact error code. Call something "not permitted" only on `AccessDenied`/`UnauthorizedOperation`.
     35	  - A cancelled, timed-out or throttled call is retried once, then reported as not completed.
     36	  - A tool refusal such as "service operations are not allowed" means: run the call in a subagent.
     37	- **Records are the deliverable** in both modes (symptoms, observations, findings, gaps, hypotheses); the last message closes them (see "Output").
     38	- **Final output.** Complete as delivered; never ends with a question or an offer. Never call `ask_user` (or any ask tool), not even after the answer to offer follow-up work or a fix: a turn that ends on a tool call loses the answer. Put follow-ups in "Next steps" and end on plain text.
     39	
     40	## Pick the mode from the request
     41	
     42	Inputs: the request text plus any incident or alarm details. A threat hunt needs no alarm. Record the mode under "Assumptions".
     43	
     44	Most requests never name WAF: they describe a symptom on a CloudFront distribution, ALB or API Gateway API and ask for the root cause or what happened. Do D-1 first. No Web ACL in the path: record `WAF_CLEARED` and continue the RCA to the actual cause (A0, "After `WAF_CLEARED`"). Otherwise classify:
     45	
     46	| Request contains | Mode |
     47	|---|---|
     48	| Denial or error symptoms: 403/405/202, empty responses, "blocked", "can't access", rejected forms, uploads or posts, a failing partner, webhook or integration, a 4xx/5xx spike, timeouts, an outage, or an alarm on a front-door resource | **Mode A**, starting with the A0 rule-out |
     49	| Suspicious traffic or hunting language: "malicious", "suspicious requests", "SQL injection", "scan", "attack", "bots", "what happened to these requests", "review WAF logs", "is WAF missing anything", a scheduled or recurring review | **Mode B** |
     50	| Both | Mode A first, then Mode B on the same window, focused on the slice Mode A found |
     51	| Neither, but the incident involves a resource that a Web ACL protects | **A0 rule-out only**; if A0 finds WAF implicated or inconclusive, continue with A1 to A7 |
     52	
     53	Mode A `CORRECT_MITIGATION`: recommend Mode B on that slice, or run it when hunting is in scope.
     54	
     55	## Defaults when input is missing
     56	
     57	Never ask; apply and record the default. Full table: "Defaults when input is missing (full table)" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     58	
     59	- **Time window:** Mode A: incident start minus 30 min through now, capped at 24 h; no incident time: last 3 h. Mode B: last 7 days.
     60	- **Web ACL:** every ACL on the resources in the request; none identifiable: all ACLs (both scopes), top 3 by denying volume.
     61	- **Several tables or log groups:** the exact location match with the newest data.
     62	- **S3 logging but no table, or no logging:** don't stop; take the degraded path and report the gap with the advisory fix.
     63	- **Missing permission:** fall back to the next source and name the permission.
     64	
     65	## Discover
     66	
     67	Read [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md) for D-1 to D-7 at the start of every run. Never ask for a resource or ACL.
     68	
     69	- **D-1 Resource to Web ACL:** CloudFront `GetDistributionConfig` `WebACLId`; regional resources `wafv2:GetWebACLForResource`.
     70	- **D-2 Read the ACL:** `wafv2:GetWebACL` for rule order, actions, managed groups and versions, `RuleActionOverrides`, Count overrides, scope-downs, custom responses, token domains, immunity times, IP set references, and any `ShieldMitigationRuleGroup_*` rule.
     71	- **D-2b Token posture:** classify P0 (no token-aware rules), P1 (token labels, no or only threshold-based enforcement) or P2 (strict token enforcement); confirm with Q-18.
     72	- **D-3 Log destination:** `wafv2:GetLoggingConfiguration`, including logging filters and redacted fields. Log group: Logs Insights. S3 or Firehose to S3: Athena. None, or a non-S3 destination without a full S3 backup: degraded path.
     73	- **D-4 Find the table or log group:** list tables in **every** Glue database, including `default`, across the Regions in D-4. Write "no table" only after that full listing. Never analyze raw log objects (`s3:GetObject`) as a substitute.
     74	- **D-7 Shield Advanced status:** `shield:DescribeSubscription`, `DescribeProtection` (L7AM status and action), `ListAttacks`/`DescribeAttack`, and `DDoSDetected` in `AWS/DDoSProtection`.
     75	
     76	**Region rule.** For CloudFront scope, the ACL, its logging configuration, its log group and its `AWS/WAFV2` metrics are in us-east-1. Only the Glue table and Athena follow the customer's setup; run Athena in the table's Region.
     77	
     78	## Bind schema and guard cost
     79	
     80	Queries are cited as `Q-NN (QA-NN / QI-NN)`; run the one for the backend from D-3 and D-4. Detail: "Schema binding and cost guards (detail)" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     81	
     82	- **Athena:** bind `<table>`, `<req>`, label type and `<pf>` from `glue:GetTable`. The log subagent reads [athena-queries.md](references/athena-queries.md) "Schema binding" and the query sections it runs.
     83	- **Logs Insights:** the log subagent reads [logs-insights-queries.md](references/logs-insights-queries.md) "Conventions" and the query sections it runs.
     84	- **Probe first, in the log subagent.** The main agent runs no Athena query. On a probe error, take the degraded path.
     85	- **Cost:** prune partitions, start narrow, no unbounded `SELECT *`, at most one `UNNEST` per query.
     86	- **Budget:** about 15 log queries (about 10 on the Mode B fast path). Report queries run and bytes scanned.
     87	
     88	## Run it in AWS DevOps Agent
     89	
     90	The main agent discovers; subagents query. Read "Subagent briefs" in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md) before you start a log subagent, and when your prompt says discovery is done.
     91	
     92	**If your prompt says discovery is done and you are a subagent:** skip Steps 1 to 3, start no further subagents and do not load this skill again. Follow "Subagent briefs" for your role.
     93	
     94	**If you are a subagent without a discovery brief** (the platform handed you the whole task, so no main agent ran Steps 1 to 3): do the main agent's and the log subagent's work yourself, and start no further log subagent.
     95	
     96	1. Do D-1 to D-4. For D-4, call `glue:GetTables` on every database that `glue:GetDatabases` returns, including `default`, and match `Location` to the log prefix. A database list alone never means "no table".
     97	2. Never analyze raw S3 log objects, or sampled requests for a window that ended over 3 hours ago.
     98	3. Run the probe, then the mode's queries. Copy each query verbatim from [athena-queries.md](references/athena-queries.md) or [logs-insights-queries.md](references/logs-insights-queries.md) by searching for its ID (for example `QA-13b`). Never summarize the query references with a distill tool: summaries drop mandatory queries.
     99	4. In Mode B, run Q-13b and Q-19 whatever else you run. In both modes, run Q-20 for a sub-rule that matches payloads (blocking or in Count).
     100	5. Return the full Output block, so the agent that started you can pass it on verbatim.
     101	
     102	- [ ] Step 1: **Main agent: discover, bind, delegate.**
     103	  - Load this skill once and no other log-search or log-analysis skill. Read reference sections by search or offset.
     104	  - Do D-1 to D-4, D-2b and `glue:GetTable` (or find the log group) yourself.
     105	  - Start **one** log-analysis subagent (`preloaded_skills: ['aws-waf-log-analysis']` where supported) and the change subagent (Step 3) in the same turn.
     106	  - The brief carries everything bound, the mode and steps, the budget and the return format; neutral wording; a unique `name` per launch.
     107	- [ ] Step 2: **Main agent: no query libraries, no log queries.** Do metrics (A1, D-5) and Shield (D-7) while the subagent runs. At most one follow-up log pass, for a new uncharacterized candidate.
     108	- [ ] Step 3: **CloudTrail only in a change subagent, never in the main agent.**
     109	  - Every `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` (A5; "After `WAF_CLEARED`"; Mode B change correlation) runs in one change subagent.
     110	  - Launch: `agent_type` `generic`, `name` `change-timeline`, `preloaded_skills: ['aws-waf-log-analysis', 'investigating-infrastructure-changes']` (whichever are available).
     111	  - Always start it, even when memory or an earlier refusal says CloudTrail is blocked; mandatory for a rule-out request.
     112	  - Its prompt points it to "Change lookups" in [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) (Regions, event names, sweep, return contract).
     113	  - Write "blocked" or "denied" only on the change subagent's own `AccessDenied`.
     114	  - No completed lookup: write "changes: not checked (<reason>)". Never "no change", "ruled out" or "CloudTrail is blocked in this environment".
     115	- [ ] Step 4: **Subagents return compact aggregates only.** Per query: ID, row count, bytes scanned, about 20 top rows; payloads as class and count; never raw result sets or log records.
     116	- [ ] Step 5: **Refusal, failure or no subagent capability.**
     117	  - Relaunch a refused log or change subagent once, under a new name, with the same `preloaded_skills`.
     118	  - Change relaunch fails too: "changes: not checked (change subagent refused twice)".
     119	  - Log relaunch fails too, or no subagents: run about 10 count-only aggregate queries yourself and record the fallback.
     120	  - A3/A4 detail is then out of reach: say so and cap confidence at "low".
     121	
     122	## Rule and label knowledge
     123	
     124	Read L-1 in [label-reference.md](references/label-reference.md) when you need a rule or label meaning (in AWS DevOps Agent, inside the log subagent).
     125	
     126	- Order: `wafv2:DescribeManagedRuleGroup` with the ACL's version when permitted (opt-in; record a denial). Then exact label strings from Q-09 (casing can differ from rule names). Then the bundled, dated tables.
     127	- A connected AWS documentation tool may confirm semantics; never required.
     128	- A label found in neither the API output nor the bundled tables is "meaning unverified". Never infer meaning from its name.
     129	
     130	## Mode A: access-denied triage
     131	
     132	Read [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) when Mode A runs (step detail), and [remediation-patterns.md](references/remediation-patterns.md) (R-01 to R-11) at Step A7.
     133	
     134	- [ ] Step A0: **WAF rule-out**, cheapest first: Web ACL in the path; symptom type fits WAF; denying metrics and Shield or Anti-DDoS signals rose; Q-15 shows denials on the scope.
     135	  - Wording alone never clears WAF (a 202 with an empty body is often reported as "timeout").
     136	  - Only "no Web ACL in the path" stops the WAF checks at once; the change subagent still runs the origin-side checks.
     137	  - `WAF_CLEARED` never ends the RCA. Origin-side next steps are checks, not conclusions; name no root cause outside WAF that evidence does not show. An origin-side change whose time matches onset and recovery is the Root Cause, with the event evidence and load-balancer metrics; never stop at "out of scope".
     138	- [ ] Step A1: **Confirm involvement:** front-door 4xx versus `AWS/WAFV2` Blocked/Challenge/Captcha per rule, against the preceding window and the prior day, with request-volume stability. Never clear WAF on 4xx alone.
     139	- [ ] Step A2: **Attribute:** group terminating records by action, rule, managed sub-rule, response code and time bucket (Q-02, Q-01, Q-14 for Shield L7AM).
     140	- [ ] Step A3: **Client capability (Challenge/CAPTCHA only):** token posture and the path's token-status profile (Q-18, Q-05, Q-09, Q-04). Quote the `failureReason` value with its count (for example `TOKEN_MISSING`).
     141	- [ ] Step A4: **Profile who is affected:** clients, URIs and match details against allowed history before onset (Q-03, Q-04, Q-06, Q-07, Q-10, Q-12, Q-13). For blocked attackers, run Q-19; never "benign" without it.
     142	  - One profile per affected client or population (Q-21): IP, user agent, country (ASN if logged), paths, blocked and allowed counts, first and last seen. Report the measured distinct client count; never assume distributed or single-source traffic.
     143	  - IP-set rule denies: read the set (`wafv2:GetIPSet`), name the matching entry, and say whether a similarly named allow set exists and which rule references it.
     144	- [ ] Step A5: **Correlate changes and events:** CloudTrail (change subagent), managed group versions, Anti-DDoS `event-detected` onset, Shield attacks (D-7). A version change or association is a cause only under the A5 evidence rules. No completed lookup: "changes: not checked".
     145	- [ ] Step A6: **Verdict** per denying (rule, action) pair: `FALSE_POSITIVE`, `CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE`, `CORRECT_MITIGATION` or `MIXED`; or overall `WAF_CLEARED` or `INCONCLUSIVE`. Give confidence (high, likely, low) and quantified impact. When legitimate users are reported denied and the logs cannot split a sub-rule's matches, the pair is `MIXED` (likely), never `CORRECT_MITIGATION`; judge request patterns, not whole clients.
     146	  - Missing allowed history is not evidence of attack. A monitor, health checker or integration with a benign profile hit by a header-presence or size rule is `FALSE_POSITIVE` (likely), with owner confirmation under "Verify before acting".
     147	  - **Payload split:** when a sub-rule (blocking or in Count) matches payloads, group its matches by pattern and field (Q-20), classify each pattern as attack or legitimate content (business text that only looks like SQL, script or JNDI), and report the split with counts ("Payload split inside one sub-rule" in [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md)).
     148	- [ ] Step A7: **Advise:** the narrowest R-xx fix, marked *reduces* or *eliminates*, validated in Count first (straight to Block only as R-01's labelled alternative).
     149	  - `CLIENT_CANNOT_SOLVE`: first a path scope-down of the challenge rule (R-05, covering every observed non-HTML path, including `/`), or token/SDK integration (R-06). Both rank above R-04.
     150	  - An IP or path is only a scope-down or exclusion on the challenge rule itself. Never add the client to an IP set used by an Allow-action rule.
     151	  - Never offer removing or disabling the Web ACL.
     152	
     153	## Mode B: threat hunting
     154	
     155	Read [threat-hunting.md](references/threat-hunting.md) when Mode B runs; classify with [threat-taxonomy.md](references/threat-taxonomy.md) at Step B6. Detected-not-blocked is a priority finding (threat labels on ALLOW, Count-mode matches, rate rules in Count, attacker residue). A logging filter that drops ALLOW records limits the analysis: say so.
     156	
     157	- [ ] Step B1: **Fast path first** for a window of 2 hours or less, or one specific question: about 10 fixed queries, started together, polled once. The full set is in "Fast path".
     158	  - Q-13b is mandatory. It sets the top talker apart so a short burst cannot hide.
     159	  - Every sensitive-path burst and every client over a rate-rule limit is a finding with method, URI, count, peaks and first to last seen. Never "ordinary", "normal" or "a retry burst".
     160	  - Run the full funnel only for candidates the fast path cannot settle.
     161	- [ ] Step B2: **B0 Known automation:** high-volume, low-diversity clients with corroboration, excluded from baselines (Q-13, Q-12, Q-01). Report them under a required "Known automation" heading. Never label them card testing or abuse. Never exclude a population with token-reuse or coordinated-activity labels.
     162	- [ ] Step B3: **B-A Overview and B-B Standouts:** time series, breakdowns and label frequency (Q-01, Q-02, Q-03, Q-09); then standouts ranked numerically (Q-08, Q-11, Q-12, Q-14, Q-16b, Q-17).
     163	- [ ] Step B4: **Attacker residue (B-B):** for every client with any BLOCK from an injection, bad-input or bot rule, report its ALLOW requests as a missed-by-rule finding (Q-19).
     164	  - Never "benign", "clean" or "accounted for" unless Q-19 showed `args_class` `none` on application paths.
     165	  - Explain a miss only from the rule's documented inspection target (L-1); otherwise "reason not determined".
     166	  - Copy the field location verbatim. A query-argument residue needs a query-string rule; a `UriPath` rule does not cover it.
     167	  - **Count-mode payload split:** for every injection or bad-input sub-rule in Count, run Q-20 and split its matches by pattern and field: the attack part is "detected, not blocked"; the legitimate-content part is a false positive that must stay unblocked.
     168	- [ ] Step B5: **B-C to B-E Drill, narrow, confirm:** re-pivot one standout; one line per Count or rate-rule client (Q-08c); narrow to one client, rule or endpoint; confirm with Q-10 or Q-16b/Q-16.
     169	  - A burst on a payment, checkout, login, signup or password-reset URI is a card-testing or credential-stuffing finding whatever its size. Fix it with a path-scoped R-10 on that URI, Count first.
     170	- [ ] Step B6: **B-F and B-G:** resolve load-bearing labels (L-1; unverified stays unverified), map each signature to a class and an R-xx mitigation, and hand legitimate-user denials to Mode A.
     171	- [ ] Step B7: **Record, then generate the hunting report.** Write the Mode B records first ("Records" under "Output"). If the runtime can create a report artifact, write the report as a Markdown artifact, following the section order and tables of [assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md](assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md) exactly; load it first:
     172	  ```
     173	  read_skill_resource(skill_id="aws-waf-log-analysis", path="assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md")
     174	  ```
     175	  - The records stay the primary deliverable; the report repeats their numbers and adds no finding.
     176	  - No artifact capability: put the same sections into the final message, after the Output template block.
     177	  - **If the `read_skill_resource` call fails**, note at the top of the report "report template (`assets/threat-hunt-report-template.md`) could not be loaded; structure follows the Mode B contract", and still produce the sections of "Output (Mode B contract)" in [threat-hunting.md](references/threat-hunting.md).
     178	
     179	## Degraded path
     180	
     181	Use when WAF logs can't be queried (no table, no logging, a non-S3 destination, a missing permission); the investigation continues. Read D-5 in [discovery-and-log-sources.md](references/discovery-and-log-sources.md).
     182	
     183	- **WAF metrics** say *whether* WAF denied and *which rule*, not *who* or *which path*. **Sampled requests:** last 3 hours only, examples rather than counts.
     184	- **Confidence:** cap at "likely" (A0 structural clears can be high). With Shield L7AM attached, a metric-based clear is `INCONCLUSIVE`. Lower to "low" when A3 or A4 cannot be assessed.
     185	- **Wrap-up:** state that WAF logs weren't analyzed and why, with the advisory fix (D-6 DDL, logging configuration, or the missing permission).
     186	
     187	## Output
     188	
     189	Read [output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md) before you write any record, handoff or final answer (record rules, last-message rules, mitigation handoff). Mode sections are in the mode references.
     190	
     191	**Template.** The main agent's very last message closes the investigation, in every mode and verdict, including any reply after the mitigation step. It starts with `Assumptions:` (no preface) and repeats this block even if earlier messages carried it:
     192	
     193	```
     194	Assumptions: window; Web ACLs; backend; mode; defaults, fallbacks, calls not completed (exact error)
     195	Verdict: <Mode A: per (rule, action), or WAF_CLEARED / INCONCLUSIVE; Mode B: per confirmed finding> (confidence: high | likely | low)
     196	Evidence: <key numbers from the log subagent's table (step-5 fallback: your recorded results), with query IDs>; Changes (CloudTrail): <per category, Regions/sources/names searched: events found | none found>; origin-side: not checked (<reason>) if not searched | not checked (<reason>) | not applicable (Mode B)
     197	AI-generated: findings need human verification before anyone acts on them.
     198	```
     199	
     200	Then the mode sections, the findings, the next steps, and a last line `Ruled out: <each hypothesis, with the evidence that closed it, or "still open">`.
     201	
     202	**Counts.** Copy every count from the log subagent's table; never recompute or round. Memory is never evidence.
     203	
     204	**Records.** Platform records are the judged deliverable in both modes. In both:
     205	
     206	- one observation record per key result first (counts, window, baseline, query ID), so findings can cite them;
     207	- exactly one Root Cause;
     208	- every Cause and Root Cause finding lists those observation IDs in its supporting observations (never empty) and the Web ACL in its related resources;
     209	- a gap record per denied or not-completed call or unassessed step; closed hypotheses with their evidence.
     210	
     211	Mode A: one symptom per burst and per affected client or population (IP, user agent, paths, blocked and allowed counts, first and last seen; never merge clients or rules); one Cause per denying (rule, action) pair, titled with the exact rule and sub-rule ID and the verdict, naming the matching resource (IP set and entry).
     212	
     213	Both modes: a payload split gives one Cause per (sub-rule, verdict), or one `MIXED` Cause listing both parts with counts, field and pattern summary.
     214	
     215	Mode B (full rules in "Mode B records" in [output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md)):
     216	
     217	- one Symptom per distinct activity pattern: window, client, method and path, counts;
     218	- one Cause per confirmed threat finding, titled with class, client and exact rule and sub-rule IDs, or "not matched by any rule", or "detected, not blocked: <rate rule> in Count";
     219	- known automation as an observation plus a closed hypothesis, never a threat finding;
     220	- the Root Cause is the overall assessment: what WAF caught, what it missed and why (for example a rate rule in Count), naming every Cause, linking their observations and any known-automation observation, with WAF-layer and Application-layer mitigations (path-scoped R-10 first for card testing; when known automation exceeds the site-wide rate rule, one sentence that it stays in Count and why).
     221	
     222	**Mitigation guardrails** (every message, finding and handoff):
     223	
     224	- Never disable or remove a rule group or the Web ACL.
     225	- Never switch a whole managed rule group, or all its sub-rules, from Count to Block, nor remove its `RuleActionOverrides` wholesale. Enforce per sub-rule, scoped to the affected path and field, with a label-based exception or scope-down for the legitimate pattern, Count first (R-01).
     226	- Card-testing or credential-stuffing burst: path-scoped R-10, not an IP exclusion.
     227	- Never add a client to an Allow IP set.
     228	- Never a site-wide rate-rule Block when known automation or shared egress exceeds the limit (R-10).
     229	- Count first.
     230	- Split WAF and application layer (R-11).
     231	- Preload `aws-waf-log-analysis` in any mitigation subagent.
     232	
     233	**Data handling.**

Use this reference when users, partners, scripts or mobile apps are denied access to an application behind AWS WAF, when error rates rise on a WAF-protected resource, or when WAF has to be ruled out during a wider outage. Steps A0 to A7 decide whether WAF caused the symptom, which rule and action did it, whether that is a false positive or a correct mitigation, and the narrowest fix.

**Rules for this mode**

- Read-only and advisory. Never change a Web ACL, rule, IP set, Shield setting or any other resource. Fixes are described in prose (see `remediation-patterns.md`).

| A0 WAF rule-out | Answer "could WAF be causing this?" with the cheapest checks first. (1) Is a Web ACL in the request path? Check CloudFront and the regional resources involved. (2) Does the symptom type fit WAF? DNS, TLS, timeout, or connection-reset failures don't, but only when the front-door telemetry shows them (the user's wording is not enough), and a custom WAF response code can make a 5xx look like an app error. (3) Did `BlockedRequests`, `ChallengeRequests`, or `CaptchaRequests` rise for the ACL in the window compared with the prior baseline? Include Shield L7AM and Anti-DDoS signals: `DDoSDetected`, `ListAttacks`. (4) If logs exist, were there denying terminations for the affected host, path, or client IP? | D-1, D-2, D-5 (metrics), D-7, Q-15 (QA-15 / QI-15). {"id": "4473bea7-73bd-4bf9-8bf1-4e2a5c9aaae3", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_XKMFTkI5EJcLyBrVmAk2OU", "content": [{"text": "## Relevant snippets

**Regions to search:**
- us-east-1 for CloudFront-scoped WAF and CloudFront events
- the ACL's Region for a regional ACL
- the origin resource's Region (from D-1: load balancer, instance or API) for security group, network ACL, route, load balancer, listener and target group events
- a rule-out or origin outage always includes the origin Region, even when the ACL is CloudFront-scoped

**CloudTrail event names to look for:**
- WAF events (us-east-1 for CloudFront-scoped ACL, otherwise the ACL's Region): `UpdateWebACL`, `UpdateRuleGroup`, `UpdateIPSet`, `UpdateManagedRuleSetVersionExpiryDate`, `PutLoggingConfiguration`, `AssociateWebACL`, `DisassociateWebACL`
- CloudFront event (us-east-1): `UpdateDistribution`
- Origin side (origin Region; only for rule-out request, `WAF_CLEARED` verdict, or timeout/5xx/outage symptom): `ModifySecurityGroupRules`, `AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress`, `RevokeSecurityGroupIngress`, `ReplaceNetworkAclEntry`, `CreateNetworkAclEntry`, `DeleteNetworkAclEntry`, `ReplaceNetworkAclAssociation`, `ReplaceRoute`, `CreateRoute`, `DeleteRoute`, `ModifyListener`, `ModifyRule`, `ModifyLoadBalancerAttributes`, `SetSecurityGroups`, `DeregisterTargets`, `RegisterTargets`, `ModifyTargetGroup`, `ModifyTargetGroupAttributes`

**Sweep methodology:**
- Write-event sweep (catch-all) runs only when per-name lookups found nothing relevant
- one `LookupAttributes` `ReadOnly`=`false` lookup per relevant Region over symptom onset -15 min to +5 min (not the whole window)
- paged, filtering `eventSource` client-side to `ec2.amazonaws.com`, `elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com`, `wafv2.amazonaws.com`, `cloudfront.amazonaws.com`
- In Mode A with WAF implicated (no rule-out request, no `WAF_CLEARED`, no timeout/5xx/outage), and in Mode B: sweep runs only in us-east-1 or ACL's Region, keeps only `wafv2` and `cloudfront`; origin Region and EC2/ELB sources are "not checked (not needed for this mode)"
- cap at 20 pages or about 5 minutes per Region; capped or early-stopped sweep reported as "incomplete (sweep capped)", not "none found"

**A5 evidence rules for version change and association:**
- Version change is a cause only when D-2 shows a pinned version that changed, or `DescribeManagedRuleGroup` / `ListAvailableManagedRuleGroupVersions` shows a new default version inside the window
- if CloudTrail shows no change and affected clients or request shapes first appear at onset (Q-04), trigger is an **input change**, and unverified version change is not listed as cause or root cause
- Association is a cause only when all three hold: resource's `webACLId` actually changed (CloudTrail request parameters or configuration history, not `LastModifiedTime` alone), logs or metrics show no requests evaluated by that ACL before it, and onset follows within minutes; otherwise do not name it, and later onset matching new clients or request shapes is an input change

**Return contract:**
- per relevant event: time, name, source, principal, source IP, user agent, Region, resource and changed values (for `UpdateDistribution`, the `webACLId` before and after)
- timeline ordered by time
- per category: Regions, event sources and names actually searched with result (for example "us-east-1 WAF/CloudFront: none found; <origin Region> EC2/ELB: `ModifySecurityGroupRules` at <time>")
- "origin-side: not checked" for any category not searched
- exact error code of any lookup that failed
- no inference from empty lookup: never "transient", "no human change" or "ruled out"

## Summary

The "Change lookups" section specifies a CloudTrail-based subagent workflow for correlating infrastructure and WAF configuration changes to symptom onset. The subagent operates across three Regions (us-east-1 for CloudFront/global resources, the ACL's Region, and the origin's Region) and performs targeted lookups on specific WAF and origin-side event names, with a catch-all write-event sweep filtered to relevant `eventSource` values when named searches return nothing. The evidence rules for causation are strict: version changes count only when pinned versions actually changed or new defaults appeared within the window; ACL associations count only when the `webACLId` provably changed, logs confirm no prior evaluation, and onset is within minutes. The return contract mandates a per-event audit trail (time, principal, changed values, exact error codes) and categorical reporting of what was searched and found, with explicit "not checked" labeling and no inferences from empty results."}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "user_reference": null}
